irac.issue: Whether the shares in question vested in the Central Government under section 3 of the Act.
irac.rule: The doctrine of Contemporanea Expositio applies only to the construction of ambiguous language in old statutes, not to modern statutes. The Court should interpret the Act based on its language and not consider extraneous matters.
irac.application: The Court rejected the attempt of the petitioners to lead the Court to consider extraneous matters, such as the background and history of the legislation, to interpret the Act. The Court held that the shares in question did vest in the Central Government under section 3 of the Act.
irac.conclusion: The Court rejected the petitioners' contention that the shares did not vest in the Central Government under section 3 of the Act.
